summary.text: A camera is an instrument that captures and stores images and video, either digitally with an electronic sensor or chemically on light-sensitive film.
Its main parts are exposure control, a lens that focuses the light, a viewfinder to preview the scene, and the film or sensor that records it.
Cameras grew from the camera obscura through 19th-century pioneers to digital models, which outsold film cameras in the United States by 2003, and then to smartphones.

facts.label: Daguerreotype
facts.value: Introduced in 1839, enabling commercial camera manufacturing

facts.label: Olympus AutoEye
facts.value: First 35mm SLR with automatic exposure, in 1960

facts.label: Digital passes film
facts.value: US digital sales overtook film by 2003

facts.label: Rangefinder cameras
facts.value: Separate viewing and imaging systems, used in photojournalism

items.prompt: A photo comes out too dark because too little light reached the sensor. Which camera part is meant to regulate that?
items.explain: Exposure control regulates the amount of light reaching the sensor or film.

items.prompt: Which camera part lets the photographer preview the scene before pressing the button?
items.explain: The viewfinder allows the user to preview the scene, while the lens focuses light and the film or sensor captures it.

items.prompt: A photographer wants to see, in real time, exactly what the lens sees. Which type of camera provides that?
items.explain: Single-lens reflex cameras provide real-time, exact imaging through the lens, unlike rangefinders, which have separate viewing and imaging systems.

items.prompt: In the late 1800s dry plates and roll-film arrived. What shift did they prompt?

options.label: Toward larger and more expensive cameras
Toward cameras that only worked in studios
Toward cameras without any lens at all
Toward smaller and more cost-effective cameras

items.explain: These advances pushed designs toward smaller, cheaper cameras, as shown by the original Kodak.

items.prompt: Why has the smartphone blurred the line between cameras and other devices?

options.label: It is easy to use, so dedicated cameras compete with a multifunctional device
It produces larger film negatives than other cameras
It replaced the lens with a pinhole
It cannot record video and so is not a camera

items.explain: Smartphone cameras are easier to use and blur the lines between dedicated cameras and multifunctional devices.

items.prompt: After World War I, which country took the lead in camera development, with precision-made cameras?

options.label: The USSR, with copied Western designs
The UK, with pocket film cameras

items.explain: Germany led after World War I, consolidating the industry and producing precision-made cameras such as the Leica and Contax.
